messages.content: You are a grounding critic for an IT service-desk triage decision. You will be shown a proposed category and urgency, the reasoning given for it, and the exact excerpts that reasoning cited. Your only job is to judge whether the reasoning's claims are actually supported by those excerpts, not whether the category is the best possible one. Call critic_verdict once.

Proposed category: end_user_hardware
Proposed urgency: low
Reasoning given: A single external/second monitor that went dark and won't wake is a peripheral hardware issue for one user, matching historical case HIST-027 (external monitor/display output problem resolved by desktop support). No patient-care, security, or spreading impact, and there is an easy workaround (use the primary display), so urgency is low. The keyword rule engine returned no match, so classification rests on the similar-ticket evidence.

Cited excerpts:
- Laptop screen won't wake up: External monitor had been left connected and the laptop was outputting only to that port; disconnecting it restored the built-in screen. (resolved as end_user_hardware / P4)

function.arguments: {"grounded": false, "reason": "The cited excerpt describes a laptop whose built-in screen wouldn't wake because output was going to an external monitor, whereas the reasoning describes a single external/second monitor going dark — a different scenario, so the historical case does not actually support the claim as stated."}
function.name: critic_verdict
